name: Pablo Picasso
hook: Cubism, Guernica, and a blue period: the modern artist Jeopardy returns to again and again.

facts.label: Guernica
facts.statement: Guernica is Picasso's 1937 answer to the bombing of a Basque town; asked by a German officer if he did it, he replied, "No, you did."

facts.label: Cubism
facts.statement: Picasso and Georges Braque founded Cubism, a movement whose three-dimensional name hides its flattening of reality onto a two-dimensional plane.

facts.label: Les Demoiselles d'Avignon
facts.statement: Les Demoiselles d'Avignon (1907) was an early Cubist landmark; its title refers to a street of ill repute in Barcelona, not a town.

facts.label: the Blue Period
facts.statement: Picasso's Blue Period followed the 1901 death of his friend Carles Casagemas and preceded his Rose Period.

facts.label: the Chicago Picasso
facts.statement: A 50-foot Cubist sculpture by Picasso stands in Chicago's Daley Plaza, unveiled in 1967; the city celebrated its 50th birthday in 2017.

facts.label: Gertrude Stein
facts.statement: Gertrude Stein and her brother Leo were early Picasso patrons; her Autobiography of Alice B. Toklas describes those friendships.
associations: The Autobiography of Alice B. Toklas

facts.label: the dove
facts.statement: Picasso drew the dove for his world-peace posters and gave the Spanish word Paloma to his daughter, who later designed Tiffany jewelry.
